podcast.title: Williams' Popularization and Characteristics
podcast.body: Hank Williams significantly popularized the Honky Tonk subgenre. Unlike the rockabilly sound pursued by artists like Johnny Cash or Elvis Presley, Williams' Honky Tonk was more traditional, focusing on working-class life and themes of disillusionment, nostalgia, and drinking. Despite its themes, it was musically cheerful and danceable, designed for the bars that gave it its name, with rhythms marked by drums and contrabass, and a characteristic Western touch from the guitar and melancholic atmosphere from the steel guitar. "El Honkittong también dio nombre a uno de los subgeneros que popoalarizó precisamente Williams. A diferencia de otros músicos que llevarían el contri hacia un sonido más roca-bili, como Johnny Cage o Elvis Presley [...] el Honkittong que él interpretaba era más a niejo."
